title: Lifecycle checkpoints for cost-and-quality-driven experiments
creator: Sofia Morales
description: Define an experiment lifecycle and concrete milestone checks that balance cost budget, latency SLOs, and qualitative output quality for A/B tests and canary rollouts. The goal is a reproducible rubric product teams can apply to scale experiments with safe, automated decision gates and clear cross-functional signoffs.
objectives: Create a 4-stage experiment lifecycle: Discovery -> Small-scale Validation -> Ramp -> Full Rollout
Define pass/fail thresholds for cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency, error rate, and prompt-quality regressions
Automate evaluation hooks that fail fast and can trigger throttles or rollback policies
Provide a lightweight checklist and templates for PMs/Eng/Design to use during run planning
milestones: M1 (Discovery, 1 week): hypothesis, target metrics, synthetic and real prompt set, risk register
M2 (Validation, 2 weeks): run 1% traffic shadow + batch eval, verify instrumentation and alerting; confirm cost baseline and latency impact
M3 (Ramp, 1 week per phase): 5% -> 20% -> 50% ramps with automated metric gates at each step
M4 (Full Rollout): production monitoring, SLA annotations, post-launch regression analysis and cost delta report
primary_metrics: Cost delta per 1k tokens (absolute and % vs baseline)
p95 latency change (ms) and percentage of requests > latency SLO
Error rate (5xx/timeout) and model failure modes (invalid JSON, hallucinations on eval set)
Quality regression score (weighted blend of automated evals + human spot checks)
acceptance_criteria: All instrumentation for metrics and traces is live and validated in staging
Automated gates evaluated and passing for at least two consecutive monitoring windows during Ramp
Stakeholder signoffs recorded: PM, Eng Tech Lead, Design, Reliability
Rollback playbook documented and verified with a simulated abort in staging
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Shadow traffic with no user-facing responses for 72 hours to validate observability
Stage 1: 1% traffic canary for 48 hours; evaluate primary metrics and human checks
Stage 2: Progressive ramp (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with 24-48 hour evaluation windows and automated gates
Stage 3: Full rollout when Ramp gates hold steady for two consecutive windows and cost/quality tolerances met
abort_criteria: Cost delta exceeds preset budget threshold (currently +30% absolute or +20% relative) for two consecutive windows
p95 latency breaches latency SLO by >25% or error rate >0.5% sustained for 30 minutes
Quality regression score drops below threshold (configured per-eval: baseline -5 points) or human review finds systematic degradation
Any security or data-exposure concern discovered during experiment
instrumentation_and_dashboards: Runtime cost dashboard (per-model, per-route) with 1h/6h/24h views
Latency SLO dashboard (p50/p95/p99) with latency percentile heatmaps
Quality regression dashboard (automated eval delta + flagged prompts)
Experiment control plane view: traffic slices, active gates, rollout stage, and rollback button
runbook_and_playbook: Step-by-step rollback instructions with traffic-shift runbook
Escalation ladder: PM -> Eng Lead -> Reliability -> CTO if incident persists
Postmortem template for experiment incidents and cost overruns
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: unexpected cost surge during Ramp; Mitigation: temporary throttle to 1% and notify billing-alert channel
Risk: unnoticed quality regression on long-tail prompts; Mitigation: seed long-tail test set and include human sampling
Risk: insufficient observability during shadow; Mitigation: require instrumentation signoff before any traffic
next_steps: Finalize evaluation thresholds and add them to experiment templates
Implement gate hooks in the experiment control plane and create dashboard filters
Run a dry-run experiment in staging using a low-risk feature to validate the lifecycle
notes: This ticket complements PM-63210 but emphasizes explicit cost/quality tradeoffs rather than solely timing and traffic pacing.
We will iterate thresholds after two internal pilots and lock defaults for the broader org by Q2 2026.
Design is working on a compact experiment summary card for Console to surface gate status and approvals.
